text:
maria: HEADS UP — after the spot node replacement in eu-west1, inference pods in namespace `inference-prod` can't reach external.model-registry.com:443, started ~2m ago.
akshat: logs?
maria: envoy logs show upstream connection failure 503, also saw DNS success but tcp to 34.12.45.67:443 resets.
jess: did the egress sidecar policy change? any new Sidecar CRs applied?
maria: not intentionally. kube events show a sidecar restart when the node drained.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: rolled out deployment inference-cache v7 -> v8 to nodepool-gpu-spot-eu-west1
akshat: suspicious — sidecar default-deny + namespace Sidecar lost ephemeral hostNetwork allowances during drain. can you paste `kubectl -n inference-prod get sidecar -o yaml` ?
maria: paste below
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: Sidecar
metadata:
  name: inference-sidecar
  namespace: inference-prod
spec:
  egress:
  - hosts:
    - "./*"
    - "mesh/*"
```
maria: it's basically only mesh and namespace local, no external hosts or ServiceEntry.
akshat: yep — default denies external. previously we had a ServiceEntry for external.model-registry.com that got deleted by a cleanup job yesterday :grimacing: 
jess: that cleanup job targeted stale serviceentries across namespaces, I acked it. we should avoid deleting prod entries.
akshat: short mitigation: add a ServiceEntry for the registry + update Sidecar to allow `external-services/*` or add `hosts: - \"*/*\"` temporarily.
maria: trying `kubectl apply -f -` with ServiceEntry
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: model-registry-ext
  namespace: inference-prod
spec:
  hosts:
  - external.model-registry.com
  addresses:
  - 34.12.45.67
  ports:
  - number: 443
    name: https
    protocol: TLS
  resolution: NONE
```
```
kubectl apply -f serviceentry.yaml
```
maria: applied, testing...
(maria reacts with :eyes:)
maria: still failing, envoy still 503s
akshat: check iptables SNAT on the node — node drain might have flipped iptables rules for CNI
`ssh node-xyz sudo iptables -t nat -L -n --line-numbers`
jess: on one replaced node iptables MASQUERADE chain missing for pod cidr
ops-bot: Node watcher: node node-xyz marked as Ready after drain
akshat: root cause likely twofold: 1) ServiceEntry deletion made sidecar block external hosts, 2) node drain dropped node-level SNAT rules temporarily; combined they caused connection resets.
maria: what permanent fix? can we patch Sidecar defaults and add guardrails around the cleanup job?
jess: propose:
- add namespace-level Sidecar with explicit hosts including `external.model-registry.com` and wildcard for external-services
- modify cleanup job to ignore resources with label `env=prod, owner=platform`
- add cluster-probe in node-rotation playbook to verify iptables MASQUERADE restored
akshat: for now I added allow for `*/*` in Sidecar egress to `inference-prod` and reapplied ServiceEntry. also opened a quick fix PR to cleanup job
maria: retesting... connections OK :white_check_mark: envoy upstream 200s now
sre-bot: Alert auto-resolve: external connection failures for inference-prod
jess: follow-ups: create runbook, add CI guard for ServiceEntry deletions, and add k8s pre-drain hook to validate SNAT
maria: thanks team, will write the postmortem and link to runbook
akshat: +1, add a Canary that simulates node rotate during deploys
maria: marking this thread for incident writeup
